Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
revision_notes: Cited source (TheGlobalEconomy.com, fetched and confirmed) reports 1.88 kbit/s per internet user for 2016, based on an older ITU series covering 2012-2016 only, correctly scored as Very Low (<5 kbit/s) at the time. A fresher ITU-derived figure was located and fetched: the ITU Digital Development Dashboard for Mali (compiled from ITU administrative ICT data collected through December 2022) reports international bandwidth per internet user at 7 kbit/s for 2019, which falls in the 5-19 kbit/s band. Score revised from 1 to 2 on this more recent evidence. No country-specific figure for Mali beyond 2019 was located; ITU only publishes aggregate LDC/LLDC averages for 2020-2022, not a Mali-specific figure, so 2019 remains the newest datable value.
revised_comments: Mali's international internet bandwidth stood at approximately 7 kbit/s per internet user in 2019, according to ITU administrative data compiled in the ITU Digital Development Dashboard. This places the country in the low-bandwidth band, well below the global average and reflecting the country's landlocked position and reliance on cross-border terrestrial fibre and satellite links for international connectivity.

Definition: The proportion of the population with basic digital skills (ability to use a computer, smartphone, or the internet for simple tasks such as sending messages, finding information, or using apps). Based on ITU household survey data, Afrobarometer, or national ICT surveys.
revision_notes: Cited source (Afrobarometer pp66 policy paper, fetched) discusses Round 7 (2016/2018) data at a Pan-African level and does not itself contain a Mali-specific '<10%' figure in the fetched text, so the original figure could not be directly confirmed from this source; it is treated as an approximation. Fresher, Mali-specific primary data was fetched from the official Afrobarometer Round 9 (fieldwork Dec 2021-Feb 2022, published 2023) national results summary for Mali, which reports internet use frequency: 57.9% never use the internet, 25.2% use it daily, 9.7% several times a week, 4.6% a few times a month, and 2.4% less than monthly (total non-never use = 42.1%). Using overall internet use as the closest available proxy for basic digital skills (consistent with the proxy approach used in the original score), this places Mali in the 40-59% band. Score revised from 1 to 4. Flagged for human review because the variable measures 'basic digital skills' specifically, while the only current country-level data available (Afrobarometer, ITU Digital Development Dashboard shows 'individuals with basic skills' as not available/NA for Mali) measures internet use frequency as a proxy, and the jump from the prior score is large.
revised_comments: Afrobarometer Round 9 (2022) survey data indicate that 42% of Malian adults use the internet at some frequency (25% daily, 10% several times a week, 5% a few times a month, 2% less than monthly), while 58% report never using it. This level of engagement suggests that a substantial minority of the population has acquired basic digital skills sufficient for simple tasks such as messaging, browsing and information search, though a majority remain offline.
